name: NFL club press and media guides, per-player prose
WHY_PROSE_AND_NOT_FIELDS: Measured 2026-09-06 over twenty guides: 3,999 field-instances carried, 3,223 already held, and of the 776 not held, 737 were the prose. College, birth date and jersey are held at 100%. A field parser would extract 39 new structured values from twenty guides. What the archive does not have is what a club publicist wrote about a man that year.
SCOPE: twenty guides, two clubs per decade 1950s-2000s, chosen so the result is checkable against that measurement. The other 1,429 are not run.

THE_BOUNDARY_IS_PROVED_NEVER_INFERRED.why: a block attached to the wrong man is undetectable and permanent. It has happened twice here and a check caught it both times: Perko's 1946 notes ran on into Tony Compagno's entry, and Wedemeyer's header split across two lines nearly merged two men.
the_proof: a span runs from one header-shaped line to the next, so it opens on a header by construction
no OTHER rostered man may appear in header position inside the span -- the Perko check, made from the roster rather than the layout
the span must carry a per-player label and be of sane length
THE_BOUNDARY_IS_PROVED_NEVER_INFERRED.header_shape_is_generic: a name-like line carrying at least two vitals signals, detected without reference to the roster, so a man the archive does not hold still breaks the span instead of being swallowed into his neighbour's entry.
THE_BOUNDARY_IS_PROVED_NEVER_INFERRED.a_split_header_is_one_header: real headers closer than 150 characters are collapsed, which is the Wedemeyer case.

THE_PROSE_IS_WHOLE_AND_VERBATIM.no_normalisation: not summarised, rewritten, normalised or OCR-corrected. The value is that a publicist chose those words; guide.Hionors is already held as printed and this follows the same rule.
THE_PROSE_IS_WHOLE_AND_VERBATIM.not_broken_into_fields: Agase's notes hold seven unrelated claims and structuring them would mean inventing a schema for 'biggest thrill'.
THE_PROSE_IS_WHOLE_AND_VERBATIM.the_guide_s_own_label_is_kept: PERSONAL, PRO, COLLEGE, TRANSACTIONS, or null for unlabelled trailing prose. These may prove to be different things and are not merged.
THE_PROSE_IS_WHOLE_AND_VERBATIM.round_trips: every block records its byte offsets and is checked character-for-character against the source file.

PER_SEASON_VITALS.what: height, weight and jersey AS THAT GUIDE PRINTED THEM, for that club-season.
PER_SEASON_VITALS.not_a_correction: 62 of 80 differ from the archive's PFA weight, median five to seven pounds. A man's weight that summer and his career-level figure are TWO FACTS. Both are held and nothing is resolved.
PER_SEASON_VITALS.cannot_overwrite: written under predicate guide.vitals_as_printed with subject person and the club-season inside the value, so it can never land on a stint or displace a career-level claim.

IDENTITY.route: club and season, which the guide establishes by construction, plus the printed name.
IDENTITY.name_rule: surname exact, forename by its first three letters within a short span, so 'John McKee (Johnny) Allen' finds Johnny Allen. NEVER surname alone: that is how a namesake takes another man's entry.
IDENTITY.unresolved: a LEAD carrying the prose, in the same structure as the other leads. Never guessed.

hard_rules: no prose block attaches to a man whose boundary was not proved
every block round-trips against its source
a per-season vital never overwrites a career-level one
no claim attaches to an unresolved man
prose is stored exactly as printed
